chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Three things I fear for my nation after me: straying after knowledge, misleading trials, and the lust of the belly and the private parts.

key_terms.الضَّلالَةُ: Straying or deviation from the truth
key_terms.شَهوَةُ الفَرجِ: Lust of the private parts (sexual desire)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things the Prophet feared most for his Ummah after his death?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights the spiritual vulnerabilities of the Ummah, particularly the danger of apostasy or confusion after possessing correct knowledge (al-dalal ba'da al-ma'rifa). It underscores the Shia emphasis on guarding against internal fitan and bodily desires (shahwat al-batin wa al-farj) which can obscure divine truth, linking the Prophet's warning to the broader eschatological context of the Twelfth Imam's occultation.
